result.lens: Front-end engineering: buildability in one self-contained HTML file with no build step — spec concreteness, real-world LCP/INP/CLS, WCAG 2.2 AA, graceful degradation, behaviour when photography is missing or uncleared, and absence of techniques that fail on contact or depend on assets/APIs we do not have.

scores.conceptName: CONCEPT 1 — Dvije Obale (Mon Ami kao tiskani list)
strengths: Only concept whose hero survives zero cleared photography. Block A is 34vh of paper with type and a rule — no image. If the photographer clearances fall through, this page still opens correctly; the other two open with a hole.

Most internally consistent token spec in the set. Every colour is given as oklch AND hex, light-dark() is used once per token, color-scheme: light dark is correctly named as mandatory, the data-theme override sets color-scheme: only light/only dark so form controls and the date picker follow, and an inline head script reads localStorage before first paint. This is the correct pattern written correctly — I can implement it from the text without a single decision of my own.
Ships the exact Google Fonts css2 URL with axis tuples and both subsets. Nobody else does this. latin-ext is correctly called non-negotiable for č ć đ š ž.

'Absence as composition' — the TARTUF panel with no photograph, the word set at 132px in gold at 18% opacity — is the single best answer to missing photography anywhere in the three concepts. It converts an asset gap into the strongest panel rather than a stock-photo apology.

Scroll-driven animation guarding is correct in both direction and default state: base rule is scaleX(1)/inset(0), the @supports wraps the animated case, and it explicitly notes animation-duration is ignored on view() timelines. Firefox users get finished, visible content.
Dialog motion names @starting-style plus transition-behavior: allow-discrete on display AND overlay — the overlay half is the bit people forget, and without it the modal snaps out of the top layer.
Static AVIF map with a text link instead of a Maps iframe: no third-party cookies on load, no iframe LCP liability, no API key.

WCAG detail is specific and correctly cited: scroll-padding-block-start for 2.4.11 via technique C43, ≥24×24 chips with 8px spacing for 2.5.8, never icon-only, real <table> for hours with aria-current='date', gold explicitly barred from text in light mode.
Column subgrid on dish rows with grid-column: 1 / -1 is the right, well-supported way to align name/leader/price across variable-length descriptions.
weaknesses: Menu 'renders from a single JS array declared at the top of the file' while the section is sold as a 'real, indexable HTML menu'. Those two claims fight each other: client-rendered rows cost CLS on a 60-row list unless contain-intrinsic-size is tuned per section, and it weakens the indexability argument that is the section's whole justification. The maintainability motive is right; the rendering strategy needs to be build-time-inlined static HTML with the array kept as the edit surface.

The fixed 5/12 hairline at z-index 0 spanning the whole document will be occluded by every full-bleed ink band (Priznanja, Dnevni ulov, footer) and will interact badly with the backdrop-filter masthead, which creates its own stacking context. Each dark band needs its own night-hairline segment — soluble, but the 'one line of CSS' claim is not true.

Bodoni Moda variable with a 6–96 opsz axis across two weights plus Instrument Sans variable, both with latin-ext, is a heavy first-party-looking payload on a page with no build step to subset it. Mitigations are named (Fontaine size-adjust fallbacks, display=swap) but the byte cost is real.

Two stacked stickies — 4.5rem masthead plus the category rail pinned at exactly 4.5rem — is correct in principle but brittle at the 3.5rem mobile header breakpoint; the rail offset must be a variable, not a literal.
content-visibility: auto on every menu section and gallery frame is specified without acknowledging its known cost: in-page anchor jumps and browser find-in-face into skipped subtrees need care.

strengths: The paired brand colour is the best accessibility idea in the whole set: Ulje as decorative-only (2.4:1, explicitly barred from small text) with Ulje-tamni as its text-safe sibling at 5.2:1. That single move lets the brand colour appear as type without a contrast waiver, and it should survive into whatever we build.

Inline SVG mini-map of the square, the bus station and a three-minute walk line is the most buildable arrival visual of the three — zero bytes of licensed raster, no API key, no cookie banner, scales perfectly, and it works today with assets we already have (coordinates).

Row subgrid — grid-template-rows: subgrid with grid-row: span 3 inside an auto-fill column grid — is the more sophisticated of the two menu techniques, aligning name/English/price baselines across independent columns. Well supported, no hacks.

Meridian mobile fallback is real graceful degradation rather than a hide: the vertical rule becomes a 2px scroll-fill bar under the header, so the device that can't carry the idea still gets the progress signal.
Lightbox view-transition-name is assigned in JS on the clicked image and cleared on finish — the correct pattern, and they know duplicate names break the transition.
Photography-inversion argument (cream ground, dark-plated food becomes the object) is coherent and slightly reduces how much the page depends on any one image being great.
weaknesses: DARK MODE: n/a — yet the palette defines Sol-noc as a dark ground, the nav spec includes a sun/moon button, the Rub token 'swaps in dark mode', and a signature move claims #ulov inverts to limewash in dark mode. The theme is referenced five times and specified zero times. I would have to invent an entire second theme, its persistence, its first-paint script and its contrast verification. That is the single biggest concreteness failure across the three.

Fraunces requested across four axes (wght, opsz, SOFT, WONK) with latin-ext and no font URL given. The multi-axis Google Fonts request syntax is fiddly and the resulting file is the largest display face proposed anywhere here — on a page whose central bet is 'h1 at opsz 144 carries a whole screen with no photograph behind it', so it is on the LCP path.

Negative text-indent to hang the comma and full stop of line two into the gutter is fragile across a 20rem→90rem fluid clamp: at some widths it clips, at others the rebalanced line breaks elsewhere and the indent lands on the wrong word. text-wrap: balance actively fights it.

Heaviest image dependency per section with the weakest fallback story: an interlocking diptych, a six-cell hand-placed masonry, the amphora frame and the sommelier frame all carry structural weight. With rights unresolved and no exterior photograph in existence, several sections have no defined degraded state.
Hero right column bleeds a 4/5 image to the viewport edge as the fetchpriority=high LCP element — same unoptimised-remote-JPEG exposure as Concept 3, without Concept 1's text-first insurance.
No first-paint theme script, no localStorage key, no color-scheme declaration anywhere — so even the light-only build inherits default form-control and scrollbar theming that fights the cream ground.

strengths: The hours object as one source of truth driving four consumers — hero chip, footer today-row, reservation time select, JSON-LD openingHoursSpecification — is the highest-value, lowest-cost engineering idea in all three concepts. It is maybe forty lines, it makes the Monday-16:30 contradiction structurally impossible, and the reservation select can never offer a slot the restaurant is closed for.

Diet filters as checkboxes plus a :has() selector on the list container: genuinely zero INP, no event handlers, no re-render, works with the keyboard for free, and degrades to 'all dishes visible' where :has() is absent. This is the right way to filter 60 rows.

Local color-scheme: light on the menu island is a sharp, correct use of the property — setting it on a subtree retints every light-dark() token inside with no duplicated rules, and the legibility argument for a dark-on-light price column is right.

Per-kilogram popover with a range input and a live tabular readout is cheap to build and removes the single most damaging number on the live menu. Highest value-per-line-of-code item anywhere in the three.
Most complete JSON-LD spec: hasMenu tree, five-decimal geo, explicit Sunday 00:00/00:00, and a stated reason for omitting aggregateRating rather than just omitting it.

Status chip colours pinned to a fixed pair verified against BOTH surfaces because the information is safety-critical and must not depend on theme state — that is a real accessibility argument, not a decorative one.
Status chip rendered on first paint from an inline script, explicitly to avoid a layout-shifting hydration artefact. Correct instinct, correctly stated.
Best risk register: names the scroll-driven opacity:0 trap, the three-family font budget with a stated drop candidate, and the maintainability handover requirement.
weaknesses: Geist Mono is not on Google Fonts. The spec says 'ONE combined Google Fonts link' for all three families; that link cannot be constructed and the build breaks on the first attempt. Self-hosting a third face in a single self-contained file means base64-inlining a woff2, which is exactly the byte cost the concept says it is avoiding.

'The real logo-monami.png with its cream background removed and re-coloured to ink via a CSS mask' does not work. mask-image keys off alpha; a PNG with a baked opaque cream ground has full alpha everywhere, so the mask paints a solid rectangle. mask-mode: luminance would render a ghost-negative, not a wordmark. Both other concepts correctly call for an SVG redraw — this one specifies a technique that fails on contact.

Most photo-dependent page of the three, with the largest exposure. A full-bleed remote JPEG is the hero LCP, plus a twelve-tile masonry, plus six dish thumbnails, plus a static map tile. With no build step to produce AVIF/WebP and rights unresolved, this is the concept that degrades worst.

The static map tile is specified as 'an SVG or a pre-rendered static tile image' — the tile half needs an API key or a licensed basemap we do not have. Concept 2's inline SVG is the version that actually ships.

Mobile action bar that hides on scroll-down adds JS scroll state to a fixed element that must never obscure focus. The spec catches the focus case, but hide-on-scroll near a form is a recurring 2.4.11 regression source and buys very little.

Three type families, eleven menu categories, two filter rows, a sticky rail with an IntersectionObserver tracker, a masonry with per-item row spans, and a lightbox — the largest surface area to get right in one file, with the least slack if any one asset is missing.

result.winner: CONCEPT 1 — Dvije Obale (Mon Ami kao tiskani list)
bestIdeasToGraft: From Concept 3: the single hours object as source of truth for FOUR consumers — the live status chip, the footer today-row highlight, the reservation dialog's time <select>, and the JSON-LD openingHoursSpecification. Concept 1 only wires it to two (chip + table). Wiring the time select to it is what makes Monday 19:00 structurally impossible to offer.

From Concept 3: diet/allergen filtering as native checkboxes plus a :has() selector on the menu container. Zero JS, zero INP, keyboard-accessible for free, and it degrades to 'everything visible'. Concept 1 has diet badges but no filter at all.

From Concept 3: the per-kilogram popover with a range input and a live tabular-nums estimate ('0,45 kg je oko 43,20 €'). Concept 1's 'po kg' pill states the unit; this one answers the actual question the guest is asking.

From Concept 3: local `color-scheme: light` on the menu subtree so a light-dark() token system retints an island with no duplicated rules. Even if the menu stays on paper in Concept 1's light mode, this is how to keep it readable as paper in dark mode instead of inverting a 60-row price column.

From Concept 3: the JSON-LD completeness — hasMenu/hasMenuSection/hasMenuItem tree, five-decimal geo, explicit Sunday 00:00:00/00:00:00, and hreflang reciprocals for hr/en/x-default. Concept 1's footer schema is thinner.

From Concept 3: rendering the status chip on first paint from a tiny inline script so it is never a layout-shifting hydration artefact — and the three-state logic including 'Otvoreno još 45 min' under an hour.
From Concept 3: fixing the open/closed chip's colour pair independent of theme, on the argument that it is safety-critical information. Adopt the rule, not just the colours.

From Concept 2: the paired brand-colour token — a decorative-only gold explicitly barred from text, plus a darkened text-safe sibling at 5.2:1. Concept 1 half-does this (oil is decoration-only in light, promoted in dark); formalising it as two named tokens prevents a stakeholder pushing gold into a caption.

From Concept 2: the inline SVG mini-map showing the square, the bus station and the three-minute walk line. Strictly better than Concept 1's static AVIF map tile — no licensed raster, no API key, no asset we do not have, scales to any DPR, and it is the only arrival visual that ships without a photographer or a mapping account.

From Concept 2: row subgrid (grid-template-rows: subgrid; grid-row: span 3) as an alternative to Concept 1's column subgrid, for any menu section that needs to flow into multiple independent columns rather than one long list.

From Concept 2: the meridian's mobile fallback — the vertical rule becomes a 2px scroll-fill bar under the sticky header below 64rem. Concept 1 simply hides its hairline on mobile; converting it to a progress rule keeps the idea alive on the device most guests use.
From Concept 2: the prev/next BUTTONS on the horizontally scrollable category rail, citing 2.5.7 — Concept 1's rail is scroll-snap only, which is a dragging-movements failure.

From Concept 2: the boxed caveat separating the restaurant's own claims (oil, medals, wine) from the MICHELIN listing. Concept 1 states the attribution rule in prose; Concept 2 puts it on the page as visible type, which is what actually protects us.
From Concept 2: the 4%-opacity tiled SVG grain overlay as an inline data URI — a few hundred bytes that stop the paper ground reading as a browser default, with no image asset required.
result.verdict:
Concept 1 wins on the one criterion that decides this project: it is the only concept that still opens correctly if the photography clearances fail. Its hero is 34vh of type and a hairline before any image appears, its most striking panel (TARTUF) deliberately has no photograph, and its gallery is seven curated frames rather than a twelve-tile masonry. Everything else we know is true about this build — remote 500KB–1.5MB JPEGs, no AVIF/WebP pipeline because there is no build step, three unsigned photographers, and no exterior shot in existence — punishes image-dependent layouts, and Concept 1 is the least image-dependent by a wide margin.

It is also the most complete spec. It is the only one that ships the actual Google Fonts URL with axis tuples and both subsets; the only one with a fully-worked theme system (light-dark() tokens, color-scheme declared, only light/only dark set from data-theme so native controls follow, inline pre-paint script, plus prefers-contrast handling); and the only one where every modern technique is described with its real gotcha attached — allow-discrete on overlay as well as display, animation-duration ignored on view() timelines, base state visible outside the @supports, @property required because gradients cannot transition. I can build it from the text without inventing anything.

Concept 3 is the better engineer and the worse front-end. Its hours-object-as-spine, :has() filters, per-kg calculator and local color-scheme island are the four best ideas in the entire set and all four must survive into the build. But it specifies two things that fail on first contact — Geist Mono is not on Google Fonts, and a CSS mask cannot strip an opaque background from a PNG (mask keys off alpha; that file has none) — and it puts a large unoptimised remote JPEG on the LCP path in a project with no image pipeline. Graft its logic, not its chrome.

Concept 2 has the best single accessibility idea (the decorative/text-safe colour pair) and the best arrival visual (inline SVG map), and both should be taken. But it declares DARK MODE: n/a while referencing dark mode in five places including a defined dark ground token and a sun/moon toggle in the nav. That is not a scope decision, it is an unfinished spec, and it sits alongside a four-axis Fraunces request with no URL and a hanging-punctuation indent that will fight text-wrap: balance across a 20rem–90rem range. Too much invention required.

Build Concept 1's structure, type system and theme; wire Concept 3's hours object into all four consumers and take its :has() filters, per-kg popover, menu-island color-scheme and JSON-LD depth; take Concept 2's paired gold tokens, inline SVG map, rail prev/next buttons and mobile meridian. Two changes to Concept 1 as specified: inline the menu as static HTML at author time with the JS array kept as the documented edit surface (client-rendering 60 rows undercuts both the CLS budget and the indexability claim the section exists to make), and give each full-bleed dark band its own hairline segment rather than relying on one fixed rule at z-index 0 to show through a backdrop-filter stacking context.
